title: Find the Most Diverse DNA Window
real_world_story: A biological research system analyzes a DNA sequence using fixed-length regions and wants to determine which region contains the greatest number of distinct nucleotide types.

real_world_connection.input_represents: A DNA sequence and the size of a region to analyze
real_world_connection.target_represents: The number of distinct nucleotide types present in the most diverse window
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Maintaining nucleotide frequencies while moving a fixed-size window across the DNA sequence

problem_statement: Given a DNA sequence and an integer K, consider every contiguous substring of length K and find the maximum number of distinct nucleotide types present in any such window.
task: Slide a window of length K across the DNA sequence and return the maximum number of distinct nucleotides found in any window.
input_format: The first line contains the DNA sequence. The second line contains an integer K representing the window size.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the maximum number of distinct nucleotides present in any window of length K.
constraints: DNA sequences contain only the characters A, C, G, and T

examples.explanation: The window 'ACG' contains three distinct nucleotides, which is the maximum for any window of length 3.
A window such as 'ACCC' contains two distinct nucleotide types, and no window contains more than two.

expected_algorithm.name: Sliding Window
expected_algorithm.reason: A fixed-size window can be moved across the DNA sequence while maintaining nucleotide frequencies, avoiding the need to recount every window from scratch.

hint: Maintain the frequency of A, C, G, and T inside the current window.
Add the new nucleotide when the window moves forward.
Remove the nucleotide that leaves the window and update the maximum number of distinct nucleotides.
real_world_takeaway: Sliding window analysis allows researchers to efficiently examine local nucleotide diversity across very large DNA sequences.
